title: Hat synthesis parameters
description: Synthesis parameters for one deterministic closed or open hi-hat sample (v0.1, proposal, #249). Mono. Only schema_version and seed are required; an omitted field takes the default named in its description. Out-of-range values are rejected, never clamped. Closed versus open is only `decay_ms` (no boolean). Time t is measured from the first sample of the sound (sample n_off with offset_ms). All numeric ranges and defaults are PROPOSALS from docs/research/2026-11-02_hat-synthesis-design.md section 4 and docs/research/2026-11-02_hat-targets-and-listening-plan.md section 2; the audio-engineer measures them and may adjust them in the engine PR (a contract-change then). Shaker, ride and stereo are not part of v0.1; they are added later by a contract-change that adds `model` values (and fields).
$comment: Contract rules that JSON Schema cannot express or that are not field ranges. (1) Cross-field rule: lp_hz must be greater than 1.2 * hp_hz. The schema cannot compare two fields, so the engine rejects a violation with an error text (never clamps) and tests check it; every default and every value of the targets-note boxes satisfies it. (2) Model `metal_bank`: bank = sum of six band-limited squares at 205.3, 304.4, 369.6, 522.7, 540 and 800 Hz times pitch_scale, each with ALL odd harmonics k with k * f < sample_rate / 2 (the rule of audio_engine.dsp.square_bank; not the 0.45 * sr cap of the kick click), all start phases 0. Noise is seeded white noise (one sub-stream per layer). Model `noise`: noise only; `metal`, `pitch_scale` and `color` are accepted and have no effect. (3) `metal` is the share of PASSBAND POWER AFTER THE HIGH-PASS CHAIN: bank and noise are each filtered by the hp_hz chain (and lp_hz, band-pass and peaking stages if used) and then RMS-normalised, and mixed as sqrt(metal) * bank + sqrt(1 - metal) * noise, so the filtered bank carries the share `metal` of the mixed power. Evidence for choosing this reading over the pre-filter reading: hypothesis H2 of the hat targets note. If the audio-engineer's render shows a correlation with the pure bank below 0.5 at metal 0.6, the engine PR documents the pre-filter reading here instead (contract-change). (4) `decay_ms` is the time from the end of the attack until the (slowest path of the) envelope has fallen 60 dB, exponential, same definition as kick amp_decay_ms. The sidecar feature `t60_ms` is the first crossing of -60 dB of the smoothed envelope and agrees with decay_ms within 10 % for body_mix 0. (5) `choke_ms` > 0 cuts the render at choke_ms after t = 0 with a 5 ms linear fade-out; samples before the fade start are identical to the same render without choke. 0 = off. A choke_ms below 5 is rejected. (6) The body path is high-passed too: hp_hz applies to the whole signal; v0.1 has no unfiltered low path. At body_mix 0 there is a single envelope with decay_ms and `decay_hi_ratio` has no effect. At body_mix > 0 the filtered mix is split by frequency at 1.5 * hp_hz (capped at 0.45 * sample_rate): the part below the split keeps the slow envelope (decay_ms), the part above gets (1 - body_mix) * slow + body_mix * fast with fast = decay_hi_ratio * decay_ms. So `body_mix` is the weight of the fast envelope on the part above 1.5 * hp_hz; it is not a level share of an oscillator group and does not select oscillators. (6a) `bp_mix` x the band-pass (bp_hz, bp_q, constant 0 dB peak gain) of the signal after the high-pass, peaking and low-pass stages is ADDED to that signal, before the RMS normalisation of (3). 0 = off. (6b) `seed` seeds only the noise: at `metal` 1 with model `metal_bank` the noise has weight 0 and `seed` has no effect on the samples; with model `noise` it always has. (7) The file ends with a 5 ms linear fade-out like the kick. Length: if length_ms is omitted the engine chooses at least decay_ms plus the fade, and the sidecar records it; a given length_ms shorter than the sound cuts it with the fade. Shared field names keep the meaning of kick-params (seed, variants, bpm, sample_rate, bit_depth, length_ms, drive, polarity, offset_ms, peak_ceiling_dbfs, preset). Engine identity for sidecars: engine.name 'abeltongod-audio-engine-hat' with the hat engine's own version (sample-metadata.schema.json, D-025).

seed.description: Seeds the noise (one sub-stream per layer). Same parameters and seed give a byte-identical WAV. Has no effect on the samples at model metal_bank with metal 1 (the noise has weight 0).

length_ms.description: File length. Omitted = chosen by the engine (at least decay_ms plus the 5 ms fade) and recorded in the sidecar. If shorter than the sound, it is cut off with a 5 ms fade-out.

model.description: metal_bank = square bank mixed with noise by `metal`. noise = noise only (metal, pitch_scale and color have no effect).

decay_ms.description: Time to fall 60 dB after the attack, exponential. Closed hats are the low part of the range, open hats the high part; there is no boolean.

metal.description: Share of passband power after the high-pass chain that comes from the square bank; the rest is noise. 0 = noise only, 1 = bank only (the seed then has no effect).

pitch_scale.description: Multiplier of the six fixed bank frequencies.

color.description: Crossfade between the low three and the high three oscillators of the bank.

hp_hz.description: Corner of the steep high-pass (two cascaded RBJ sections), Hz. lp_hz must be greater than 1.2 * hp_hz.

lp_hz.description: Corner of the low-pass, Hz. Must be greater than 1.2 * hp_hz (cross-field rule, checked by the engine).

bp_hz.description: Centre of the band-pass emphasis path, Hz.

bp_q.description: Q of the band-pass emphasis path.

bp_mix.description: Weight of the band-pass path that is added to the signal: output = signal + bp_mix * bandpass(signal), the band-pass having 0 dB peak gain at bp_hz. 0 = off.

peak_hz.description: Centre of a static peaking filter, Hz. No effect at peak_db 0.

peak_db.description: Gain of the peaking filter, dB. 0 = off.

body_mix.description: Weight of the fast envelope (decay_hi_ratio * decay_ms) on the part of the signal above 1.5 * hp_hz; the part below that split keeps the slow envelope (decay_ms). Not a level share of an oscillator group. 0 = single envelope (decay_hi_ratio has no effect).

decay_hi_ratio.description: Decay of the fast envelope (applied above 1.5 * hp_hz) relative to decay_ms. Only used when body_mix > 0.

drive.description: Anti-aliased saturation, same stage as kick drive. 0 = off.

choke_ms.description: 0 = off; otherwise the render is cut at this time (ms after t = 0) with a 5 ms fade-out. Values between 0 and 5 are rejected.

polarity.description: Sign of the whole output, applied after the peak ceiling.

offset_ms.description: Silence before the sound, rounded to whole samples (as in kick-params).

peak_ceiling_dbfs.description: Peak ceiling of the quantised file.

preset.description: Name of the preset these values came from, if any.
